blocks.t: F i g u r e 16.8 The calcium carbonate in marble and limestone is very slightly soluble in neutral water. Its solubility is much greater in acidic water. Objects carved of these ma­te­rials dissolve relatively rapidly in areas where rain, snow, or fog is acidified from air pollution. Shown here is the damage to a marble statue of George Washington between 1935 (left) and 1994 (right).

As the solution is made more acidic, the concentration of hydroxide ion decreases, causing an increase in the concentration of Zn21(aq) ion. Zinc hydroxide is thus more soluble in acidic solution than in pure water.
